facts.function: Strut holding limb away from trunk; transmits limb forces to axial skeleton; most commonly fractured bone (middle third)
facts.attachments: Sternoclavicular joint medially, acromioclavicular joint laterally; coracoclavicular ligament inferiorly; SCM, pectoralis major, deltoid, trapezius

facts.function: Anterior midline thoracic bone; manubrium gives the only bony link of upper limb to axial skeleton
facts.attachments: Manubrium, body, xiphoid; manubrium articulates with clavicles and 1st costal cartilages; sternal angle at 2nd rib

facts.function: Mobile base for the upper limb; glides on posterior thorax (ribs 2–7); anchors rotator cuff
facts.attachments: Glenoid articulates with humeral head; acromion with clavicle; coracoid anchors pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis, short head biceps

facts.function: Divides posterior scapula into supraspinous and infraspinous fossae; continues laterally as acromion
facts.attachments: Trapezius inserts on superior lip; posterior (spinal) deltoid arises from inferior lip

facts.function: Fossa above scapular spine housing supraspinatus; suprascapular nerve and artery pass through
facts.attachments: Origin of supraspinatus; suprascapular nerve passes under, artery over, superior transverse scapular ligament

facts.function: Fossa below scapular spine housing infraspinatus
facts.attachments: Origin of infraspinatus; suprascapular nerve and artery reach it via spinoglenoid notch

facts.function: Lateral end of scapular spine forming point of shoulder; roofs GH joint with coracoacromial ligament
facts.attachments: Articulates with lateral clavicle (AC joint); middle deltoid origin; trapezius insertion

facts.function: Hook-like anterior scapular process; muscle and ligament anchor palpable below lateral clavicle
facts.attachments: Pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis, short head of biceps; coracoclavicular and coracoacromial ligaments

facts.function: Shallow socket of GH joint deepened by labrum; shallowness permits mobility but favors dislocation
facts.attachments: Articulates with humeral head; supraglenoid tubercle = long head biceps; infraglenoid tubercle = long head triceps

facts.function: Arm bone; fracture-nerve pairs: surgical neck–axillary, midshaft–radial, supracondylar–median, medial epicondyle–ulnar
facts.attachments: Head articulates with glenoid; trochlea with ulna; capitulum with radius

facts.function: Hemispherical articular surface of proximal humerus; anterior dislocation most common
facts.attachments: Articulates with glenoid cavity; bounded by anatomical neck
facts.supply: Anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries

facts.function: Groove just beyond articular head marking former epiphyseal line; fractures rare
facts.attachments: Attachment of glenohumeral joint capsule

facts.function: Narrowing distal to tubercles; common fracture in elderly, risking axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
Lateral proximal humeral prominence; insertion of three rotator cuff muscles
facts.attachments: Superior, middle, inferior facets: supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor

facts.function: Anterior proximal humeral prominence; insertion of the only anterior rotator cuff muscle
facts.attachments: Subscapularis inserts here

facts.function: Groove between tubercles transmitting long head of biceps tendon, held by transverse humeral ligament
facts.attachments: Lateral lip: pectoralis major; floor: latissimus dorsi; medial lip: teres major (lady between two majors)

facts.function: Spiral groove on posterior humerus carrying radial nerve and deep brachial artery; midshaft fracture → wrist drop
facts.attachments: Separates origins of lateral head (above) and medial head (below) of triceps

facts.function: Spool-shaped medial articular surface of distal humerus forming humeroulnar hinge
facts.attachments: Articulates with trochlear notch of ulna

facts.function: Rounded lateral articular surface of distal humerus forming humeroradial joint
facts.attachments: Articulates with head of radius

facts.function: Non-articular distal humeral projections; ulnar nerve runs behind medial epicondyle (funny bone)

facts.function: Proximal ulnar projection forming point of elbow; fits olecranon fossa in extension
facts.attachments: Insertion of triceps brachii; anconeus attaches laterally

facts.function: Ulnar notch between olecranon and coronoid process that grips the trochlea (humeroulnar hinge)
facts.attachments: Articulates with trochlea of humerus

facts.function: Transmits axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery
facts.attachments: Teres minor (superior), teres major (inferior), long head triceps (medial), surgical neck of humerus (lateral)

facts.function: Transmits circumflex scapular artery
facts.attachments: Teres minor (superior), teres major (inferior), long head of triceps (lateral)

facts.function: Transmits radial nerve and deep brachial artery into posterior arm
facts.attachments: Teres major (superior), long head triceps (medial), lateral head triceps or humerus (lateral)

facts.function: Contains, lateral→medial, radial nerve, biceps tendon, brachial artery, median nerve; median cubital vein superficial for venipuncture
facts.attachments: Bounded by interepicondylar line (superior), brachioradialis (lateral), pronator teres (medial); roof is bicipital aponeurosis

facts.function: Saddle synovial joint with articular disc; only bony joint linking upper limb to axial skeleton
facts.attachments: Medial clavicle ↔ manubrium and 1st costal cartilage; costoclavicular ligament is main stabilizer

facts.function: Plane synovial joint letting scapula glide and rotate on clavicle; injured in shoulder separation
facts.attachments: Lateral clavicle ↔ acromion; stabilized by acromioclavicular and coracoclavicular ligaments

facts.function: Ball-and-socket joint; most mobile and most often dislocated joint (usually anteroinferior)
facts.innervation: Axillary, suprascapular, and lateral pectoral nerves
facts.attachments: Humeral head ↔ glenoid cavity; stabilized by capsule, labrum, glenohumeral ligaments, and rotator cuff
facts.supply: Anterior and posterior circumflex humeral and suprascapular arteries

facts.function: Physiologic (non-synovial) joint; scapular gliding on thorax gives ~1/3 of arm abduction (2:1 scapulohumeral rhythm)
facts.attachments: Scapula ↔ posterior thoracic wall, with serratus anterior and subscapularis between

facts.function: Fibrocartilage rim deepening the glenoid; SLAP tear superiorly, Bankart lesion anteroinferiorly after dislocation
facts.attachments: Glenoid rim; superiorly continuous with long head of biceps tendon

facts.function: Strengthens AC joint capsule superiorly; resists horizontal displacement
facts.attachments: Acromion ↔ lateral end of clavicle

facts.function: Main vertical stabilizer of AC joint; suspends scapula from clavicle; torn in high-grade separations
facts.attachments: Coracoid process ↔ inferior clavicle; conoid (medial) and trapezoid (lateral) parts

facts.function: Completes coracoacromial arch; prevents superior displacement of humeral head
facts.attachments: Coracoid process ↔ acromion

facts.function: Roof over GH joint; supraspinatus tendon and subacromial bursa pass beneath (impingement site)
facts.attachments: Acromion, coracoid process, and coracoacromial ligament

facts.function: Anchor and position the scapula on the thorax for upper limb movement
Superior fibers elevate, middle retract, inferior depress scapula; superior plus inferior upwardly rotate
facts.innervation: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI); C3–C4 proprioception
facts.attachments: Occipital bone, nuchal ligament, C7–T12 spinous processes → lateral clavicle, acromion, spine of scapula

facts.function: Elevates scapula and rotates glenoid inferiorly
facts.innervation: Dorsal scapular nerve (C5) and cervical nerves C3–C4
facts.attachments: Transverse processes C1–C4 → superior medial border of scapula

facts.function: Retracts scapula, rotates glenoid inferiorly, fixes scapula to thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Spinous processes T2–T5 → medial border of scapula below spine

facts.function: Retracts scapula, rotates glenoid inferiorly, fixes scapula to thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Nuchal ligament, spinous processes C7–T1 → medial border at root of scapular spine

facts.function: Protracts and upwardly rotates scapula, holding it to thorax; paralysis → winged scapula
facts.attachments: External surfaces of ribs 1–8 → anterior surface of medial border of scapula

facts.function: Stabilizes, depresses, and protracts scapula; landmark dividing axillary artery into three parts
facts.attachments: Ribs 3–5 near costal cartilages → coracoid process

facts.function: Initiates arm abduction (first ~15°); rotator cuff stabilizer; most commonly torn cuff tendon (impingement)
facts.attachments: Supraspinous fossa → superior facet of greater tubercle

facts.function: Laterally rotates arm; rotator cuff stabilizer of GH joint
facts.attachments: Infraspinous fossa → middle facet of greater tubercle

facts.function: Laterally rotates and weakly adducts arm; rotator cuff stabilizer
facts.attachments: Middle lateral border of scapula → inferior facet of greater tubercle
facts.supply: Circumflex scapular and posterior circumflex humeral arteries

facts.function: Medially rotates and adducts arm; anterior rotator cuff stabilizer
facts.attachments: Subscapular fossa → lesser tubercle

facts.function: Acromial part abducts arm 15–90°; clavicular part flexes and medially rotates; spinal part extends and laterally rotates
facts.attachments: Lateral clavicle, acromion, spine of scapula → deltoid tuberosity of humerus
facts.supply: Posterior circumflex humeral artery and deltoid branch of thoracoacromial artery

facts.function: Adducts and medially rotates arm; clavicular head flexes, sternocostal head extends the flexed arm
facts.attachments: Medial clavicle, sternum, costal cartilages 1–6, external oblique aponeurosis → lateral lip of intertubercular groove

facts.function: Extends, adducts, and medially rotates arm (climbing, swimming)
facts.attachments: T7–T12 spinous processes, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, lower ribs → floor of intertubercular groove

facts.function: Adducts and medially rotates arm
facts.attachments: Posterior inferior angle of scapula → medial lip of intertubercular groove

facts.function: Anterior rami of C5–T1 forming the plexus; give dorsal scapular (C5) and long thoracic (C5–C7) nerves
facts.innervation: Mixed motor and sensory fibers of spinal nerves C5–T1
facts.attachments: Emerge between anterior and middle scalenes with subclavian artery → unite into trunks

facts.function: Union of C5–C6; gives suprascapular nerve and nerve to subclavius; injury = Erb palsy (waiter's tip)
facts.attachments: Anterior division → lateral cord; posterior division → posterior cord

facts.function: Continuation of the C7 root alone
facts.attachments: Anterior division → lateral cord; posterior division → posterior cord

facts.function: Union of C8–T1; injury = Klumpke palsy (claw hand), e.g., grabbing a branch, Pancoast tumor, cervical rib
facts.attachments: Anterior division → medial cord; posterior division → posterior cord

facts.function: Gives lateral pectoral nerve, musculocutaneous nerve, and lateral root of median nerve
facts.innervation: C5–C7; from anterior divisions of superior and middle trunks
facts.attachments: Lies lateral to 2nd part of axillary artery, deep to pectoralis minor

facts.function: Gives medial pectoral, medial brachial and antebrachial cutaneous, ulnar nerve, and medial root of median
facts.innervation: C8–T1; anterior division of inferior trunk
facts.attachments: Lies medial to 2nd part of axillary artery, deep to pectoralis minor

facts.function: Gives upper and lower subscapular, thoracodorsal, axillary, and radial nerves (ULTRA)
facts.attachments: Lies posterior to 2nd part of axillary artery

facts.function: Motor to anterior arm (coracobrachialis, biceps, brachialis); sensory to lateral forearm via lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve
facts.attachments: Pierces coracobrachialis, runs between biceps and brachialis, emerges lateral to biceps tendon

facts.function: Motor to deltoid and teres minor; sensory over lateral shoulder; injured in surgical neck fracture or anterior dislocation
facts.attachments: Through quadrangular space with posterior circumflex humeral artery, winding around surgical neck

facts.function: Motor to posterior arm and forearm extensors; sensory to posterior arm, forearm, dorsolateral hand; midshaft fracture → wrist drop
facts.innervation: C5–T1, terminal branch of posterior cord
facts.attachments: Triangular interval → radial groove with deep brachial artery → anterior to lateral epicondyle → superficial and deep branches

facts.function: Motor to most forearm flexors, thenar muscles, lateral lumbricals; sensory to lateral palm and 3½ digits
facts.innervation: C5–T1, from lateral and medial cord roots
facts.attachments: With brachial artery in arm (no branches) → between pronator teres heads → deep to FDS → carpal tunnel

facts.function: Motor to FCU, medial FDP, most intrinsic hand muscles; sensory to medial 1½ digits; injury → claw hand
facts.attachments: Medial arm (no branches) → behind medial epicondyle (cubital tunnel) → between FCU heads → Guyon's canal

facts.function: Motor to serratus anterior; injury (axillary node dissection, mastectomy) → winged scapula
facts.attachments: Descends behind brachial plexus onto superficial surface of serratus anterior on lateral thoracic wall

facts.function: Motor to rhomboids and part of levator scapulae
facts.attachments: Pierces middle scalene, descends deep to levator scapulae and rhomboids along medial scapular border

facts.function: Motor to supraspinatus and infraspinatus; sensory to GH and AC joints
facts.attachments: Through suprascapular notch beneath superior transverse scapular ligament → around spinoglenoid notch

facts.function: Motor to pectoralis minor and sternocostal part of pectoralis major
facts.attachments: Pierces pectoralis minor to reach pectoralis major

facts.function: Motor mainly to pectoralis major (clavicular head); some fibers reach pectoralis minor
facts.attachments: Pierces clavipectoral fascia to reach deep surface of pectoralis major

facts.function: Motor to latissimus dorsi; at risk in axillary surgery
facts.attachments: Descends along posterior axillary wall with thoracodorsal artery

facts.function: Motor to superior part of subscapularis
Motor to inferior part of subscapularis and teres major
Supinates forearm (strongest with elbow flexed) and flexes elbow; weakly flexes shoulder
facts.attachments: Long head supraglenoid tubercle; short head coracoid → radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis

facts.function: Flexes elbow, supinates forearm; tendon in intertubercular groove helps hold humeral head down
facts.attachments: Supraglenoid tubercle and superior labrum, through GH joint → radial tuberosity

facts.function: Flexes elbow, supinates forearm; assists shoulder flexion
facts.attachments: Tip of coracoid process (with coracobrachialis) → radial tuberosity

facts.function: Main flexor of the elbow in all forearm positions
facts.innervation: Musculocutaneous nerve (C5–C6); small lateral part by radial nerve
facts.attachments: Distal anterior humerus → coronoid process and ulnar tuberosity

facts.function: Flexes and adducts arm
facts.attachments: Tip of coracoid process → middle of medial humerus

facts.function: Main extensor of elbow; long head also extends and adducts arm
facts.attachments: Infraglenoid tubercle and posterior humerus → olecranon

facts.function: Extends elbow; crosses shoulder to extend and adduct arm; borders quadrangular and triangular spaces
facts.attachments: Infraglenoid tubercle of scapula → olecranon

facts.function: Extends elbow; strongest for forceful extension
facts.attachments: Posterior humerus above radial groove → olecranon

facts.function: Extends elbow; workhorse active in all extension
facts.attachments: Posterior humerus below radial groove → olecranon

facts.function: Humeroulnar and humeroradial hinge flex/extend elbow; proximal radioulnar pivot allows pronation/supination; one shared capsule
facts.attachments: Trochlea–trochlear notch; capitulum–radial head; radial head–radial notch of ulna
facts.supply: Elbow anastomosis of collateral (brachial, deep brachial) and recurrent (radial, ulnar, interosseous) arteries

facts.function: Collateral ligaments resist varus/valgus stress; annular ligament holds radial head against ulna
Resists valgus stress; anterior band injured in throwing athletes (Tommy John repair)
facts.attachments: Medial epicondyle → coronoid process and olecranon of ulna

facts.function: Resists varus stress; lateral elbow stabilizer
facts.attachments: Lateral epicondyle → blends with annular ligament

facts.function: Encircles radial head in radial notch; radial head subluxation = nursemaid's elbow
facts.attachments: Anterior and posterior margins of radial notch of ulna

facts.function: Supplies upper limb, plus brain (vertebral), neck, and thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Right from brachiocephalic trunk, left from aortic arch; between anterior and middle scalenes → axillary at 1st rib lateral border

facts.function: Supplies supraspinatus and infraspinatus; part of scapular anastomosis
facts.attachments: Branch of thyrocervical trunk → passes over superior transverse scapular ligament

facts.function: Supplies rhomboids, levator scapulae, trapezius; part of scapular anastomosis
facts.attachments: Branch of subclavian artery or deep branch of transverse cervical artery → along medial border of scapula

facts.function: Supplies shoulder, axillary walls, lateral thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Subclavian at lateral border of 1st rib → brachial at inferior border of teres major; pectoralis minor divides it into 3 parts

facts.function: Supplies 1st–2nd intercostal spaces and superior serratus anterior
facts.attachments: Only branch of 1st part of axillary artery

facts.function: Supplies pectoral muscles, deltoid, acromion, clavicle
facts.attachments: 2nd part of axillary; pierces clavipectoral fascia → pectoral, acromial, clavicular, deltoid branches

facts.function: Supplies serratus anterior, pectoral muscles, lateral breast
facts.attachments: 2nd part of axillary artery → descends along lateral border of pectoralis minor

facts.function: Largest axillary branch; supplies subscapularis, latissimus, teres major; major scapular anastomosis contributor
facts.attachments: 3rd part of axillary artery → circumflex scapular and thoracodorsal arteries

facts.function: Supplies muscles on dorsal scapula; scapular anastomosis with suprascapular and dorsal scapular arteries
facts.attachments: Branch of subscapular artery → through triangular space to infraspinous fossa

facts.function: Supplies latissimus dorsi
facts.attachments: Continuation of subscapular artery; accompanies thoracodorsal nerve

facts.function: Supplies humeral head and shoulder joint
facts.attachments: 3rd part of axillary → winds anterior to surgical neck → anastomoses with posterior circumflex humeral

facts.function: Supplies deltoid, teres minor, GH joint; injured with axillary nerve in surgical neck fracture
facts.attachments: 3rd part of axillary → quadrangular space with axillary nerve → around surgical neck

facts.function: Main artery of arm supplying anterior compartment; site of blood pressure measurement
facts.attachments: Axillary at inferior border of teres major → with median nerve → radial and ulnar arteries in cubital fossa

facts.function: Supplies posterior compartment (triceps); contributes to elbow anastomosis
facts.attachments: Proximal brachial branch → radial groove with radial nerve → middle and radial collateral arteries

facts.function: Paired venae comitantes draining deep structures of the arm
facts.attachments: Accompany brachial artery → join basilic vein to form axillary vein

facts.function: Superficial vein draining medial hand, forearm, and arm
facts.attachments: Ulnar dorsal venous network → medial forearm and arm → pierces deep fascia → joins brachial veins forming axillary vein

facts.function: Superficial vein draining lateral hand, forearm, and arm
facts.attachments: Radial dorsal venous network → lateral arm → deltopectoral groove → pierces clavipectoral fascia → axillary vein

facts.function: Drains upper limb, axilla, and lateral thoracic wall
facts.attachments: Basilic plus brachial veins at teres major → subclavian vein at 1st rib; lies medial to axillary artery

facts.function: Drains upper limb; common central venous access site
facts.attachments: Axillary vein at 1st rib → anterior to anterior scalene → joins internal jugular forming brachiocephalic vein
